coverage_of_risk.rationale: No tests were written at all, despite the vitest/jsdom/`@angular/build:unit-test` infrastructure being installed and configured. The riskiest logic — data transformation, sorting, pagination, URL state — is entirely uncovered.

findings.issue: Zero unit tests despite fully configured test infrastructure: `ng test` script (app/package.json:19), @angular/build:unit-test builder (app/angular.json:75-76), vitest and jsdom in devDependencies. The scaffolding was created and then never used.
findings.suggestion: Add at minimum unit specs for util.ts, catalog.service.ts's pokemonRefsToCards, the pokemonResolver's move-table assembly, and MoveTableComponent's sorting — all are pure or near-pure logic that vitest can cover without an HTTP server.

findings.issue: pokemonRefsToCards encodes the trickiest invariants in the app — id>=10000 alternate-form exclusion (:124), species remapping for form names like deoxys-normal (:126), dedup with hidden-flag merging (:130-133), dex-number ordering (:144) — and every 'Learned by'/'Pokémon with type X' list flows through it untested.
findings.suggestion: A table-driven spec with a small fake catalog covering: alternate form dropped, form name remapped to species, duplicate refs deduped, hidden flag merged, output sorted by id.

findings.issue: The moves-section assembly is fragile: the method-order comparator at :193-199 mixes indexOf and length sentinels (easy to invert), rows are pushed once per level_learned_at (:211-218, potential duplicates), and the default sort (:221-224) switches strategy between level-up and other methods. A refactor of the data layer here breaks level ordering, method ordering, or the level column silently.
findings.suggestion: Spec the resolver against fixture pokemon/move/version-group payloads: assert selected-game fallback (:167-170), method table order (Level Up, Machine, Egg, Tutor, then alphabetical), and per-table default ordering including ties.

findings.issue: compareValues must keep missing values last in BOTH directions — the classic bug is nulls flipping to the front when direction flips because the null checks are applied before the direction sign. No test pins this invariant, and the aria-sort/toggle state machine (:105-115) is also untested.
findings.suggestion: A pure-function spec on the comparator (or a component test clicking the Power header twice) would lock the behaviour cheaply.

findings.issue: Pagination and URL state are only guarded by the acceptance suite's exact URLs: parseInt fallback for garbage ?page values (:44-45), clamping past the last page (:46), query-param omission at defaults (:83-92). Subtle regressions (page=0, page=999, non-numeric) would slip through once the Playwright suite is refactored away.
findings.suggestion: Component-level specs feeding the q/type/generation/page inputs and asserting filtered/pageItems/totalPages outputs would cover every edge in milliseconds.

findings.issue: The module-level response cache has two easily-broken invariants: failed requests must be evicted so a retry can succeed (:55-58), and normalize()'s trailing-slash logic (:63-66) must not double-slash query paths. Also, the cache is process-global across all SSR requests, so a leak here serves stale data to every user.
findings.suggestion: Spec with a stubbed HttpClient: cached promise reused, error evicted (second get refetches), and normalize('pokemon/25') vs normalize('type?limit=100') URL shapes.

findings.issue: The five spec-defined formatting helpers (humanize word splitting, whitespace collapsing in latestEnglishFlavor, 4-digit padding, em-dash fallback) are exactly the kind of pure functions that invite 'harmless' refactors and exactly the kind tests are for. humanize on empty segments ('-x-' style names) and latestEnglishFlavor's /\s+/g collapse are both edge-case-prone.
findings.suggestion: One spec file, ~30 lines, covering the SPEC's own examples (mr-mime → Mr Mime, #0025, — for null).

findings.issue: The SSR 404 path (RESPONSE_INIT status mutation in the constructor) and the resolver null-handling that routes unknown /pokemon/:name to a 404 (app/src/app/page-data.ts:160-165) are untested; a resolver that starts throwing instead of returning null would render a crash page rather than a 404.
findings.suggestion: A routing test that resolves an unknown name and asserts the NotFoundComponent renders plus the effect-based title falls back (app/src/app/pokemon.page.ts:33-36).

summary: The agent shipped a well-built app with zero tests of its own, leaving the vitest/jsdom infrastructure it installed completely unused. All the highest-risk logic — catalog assembly, card mapping, move-table grouping and sorting, pagination and URL state, the HTTP cache — is guarded only by the external acceptance suite, so any refactor of the data layer will be flying blind. Given how much of this logic is pure and trivially testable, the omission is a clear gap rather than a cost trade-off.

untested.likelyBug: Alternate forms leaking into 'Learned by' lists, form names (deoxys-normal) linking to /pokemon/deoxys-normal instead of the species, or hidden-ability flags lost during dedup.
Method tables ordered wrong after a comparator tweak, ?game= fallback breaking when the query param names an unknown game, or duplicate rows for moves with multiple level entries.
Null power/accuracy rows flipping to the front on descending sort, or aria-sort applied to the wrong column after a toggle refactor.
Out-of-range or non-numeric ?page values producing an empty list instead of clamping; filters no longer resetting to page 1; debounce timer firing after navigation and clobbering the URL.
